methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective single-center cohort design (203 patients at one tertiary hospital, 2017-2023) is appropriate for descriptive and prognostic questions but inherently limits generalizability, as the authors acknowledge. Strengths include use of landmark analysis at 3 and 6 months to mitigate immortal time bias, pre-specified criteria (CHAARTED) for high-volume disease, dual-radiologist review of imaging, and comparison of included vs. lost-to-follow-up patients (Supplementary Table 1). Weaknesses: no a priori power calculation; the exposed group for docetaxel at 3 months is only n=12 (acknowledged); univariate variable selection at p<0.2 followed by multivariable Cox without stepwise selection is reasonable but no sensitivity analyses, no propensity score matching for treatment comparisons despite acknowledged selection bias, and no competing-risks or validation cohort. PSA was analyzed only categorically (per manuscript, >70% had no continuous value), limiting modeling of a key prognostic variable, and the counterintuitive 'protective' effect of PSA≥100 ng/mL is likely residual confounding. Multiplicity across multiple landmark/treatment tests was not corrected.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study (Oxford LoE 2b). Clinical relevance is moderate: the question (prognostic determinants and treatment timing in SBM-HSPC) is clinically important, uses the patient-relevant endpoint of overall survival, and the finding that early NHA initiation (≤3 months) is associated with a 45% mortality reduction aligns with and reinforces TITAN/LATITUDE/ENZAMET recommendations, potentially supporting advocacy for timely intensive therapy in Chinese practice. However, the association is confirmatory rather than practice-changing (NHA benefit is already guideline-established), the single-center setting constrains translational reach, and the counterintuitive PSA finding and borderline age/smoking signals are hypothesis-generating only. The contemporary Chinese prevalence estimate (6.09%) has regional epidemiologic value.

reporting_quality.justification: As an observational cohort study, STROBE is the applicable checklist. Reporting covers most key STROBE items: eligibility criteria, variable definitions (including structured definitions for SRE ascertainment and bone metastasis assessment), setting, follow-up definition, missing-data policy (complete-case, <5% missingness), a described patient-flow process (Figure 1), and acknowledgement of limitations. Gaps: no explicit STROBE checklist, no a priori sample-size justification, no protocol registration, limited reporting of confidence intervals for descriptive comparisons, and no formal bias/confounding discussion in a structured manner. There is no data-availability statement, no code sharing, and no repository identifier visible in the blinded text; the methods lack sufficient scripts/protocols for independent replication—hence a low data-availability score.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily empirical/population-based: a contemporary single-center Chinese prevalence of SBM-HSPC (6.09%) and a landmark-analysis-based real-world association between early NHA initiation and OS. The core therapeutic finding (NHA benefit in mHSPC) is well-established by TITAN, LATITUDE, ENZAMET, ARASENS, and PEACE-1, which the authors directly cite as comparators. The methodological approach (Cox + landmark) is standard; no new biomarker, mechanism, or trial design is introduced. The regional epidemiologic update and timing-focused observational signal are incremental confirmations of known findings in an underreported Chinese tertiary-center population.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized conventionally (intro–methods–results–discussion–conclusions), the abstract is quantitatively grounded and reflects the main findings, and the discussion is appropriately cautious about the paradoxical PSA association and the sources of temporal prevalence decline. Weaknesses include minor grammatical issues ('age 60–74 years as protective', 'was l associated with', 'Smoking statuse', inconsistent spacing around parentheses), occasional overlap between results and discussion, speculative framing in the introduction (e.g., 'we speculate that the proportion…in 2008 was significantly higher than the reported 58%' conflicts with the manuscript's own earlier figure of 54%), and figure/table captions that are overly terse (e.g., Figure 2 caption only states 'median survival time'). Reference list formatting is irregular. Overall adequate for peer review but requires copyediting.

key_strengths: Use of 3- and 6-month landmark analysis to mitigate immortal time bias when evaluating early NHA initiation
Pre-specified CHAARTED criteria for high-volume disease and structured dual-reviewer adjudication of bone metastases and SREs
Transparent, appropriately cautious discussion of the counterintuitive PSA≥100 ng/mL association, including explicit data limitations
Comparison of included vs. lost-to-follow-up patients demonstrating no significant baseline differences
Contemporary Chinese tertiary-center prevalence estimate (6.09%) that updates older multicenter figures
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with 203 patients and no a priori power calculation; subgroup exposures (e.g., docetaxel n=12 at 3-month landmark) underpowered
PSA modeled only categorically because continuous values were unavailable for >70% of high-PSA patients, producing an uninterpretable 'protective' effect for PSA≥100 ng/mL
Treatment-timing comparisons are observational without propensity-score adjustment, competing-risks analysis, sensitivity analyses, or multiplicity correction
Core therapeutic finding (early NHA benefit) is confirmatory of TITAN/LATITUDE/ENZAMET/ARASENS rather than novel
No data-availability or code-sharing statement; STROBE checklist not explicitly addressed and no protocol registration
Writing requires copyediting (grammar, inconsistent prevalence figures 54% vs. 58%, terse figure captions)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently conducted but incremental single-center retrospective cohort that confirms established NHA guidelines in a Chinese population; appropriate for a tier-3 oncology journal after major revisions addressing the PSA handling, confounding, and reporting-standard gaps.
